concepts.prompt: Game item concept: the game's Tether capture orb, redesigned from the reference orb (same carved-stone and brass craftsmanship, same art style). A perfect sphere made of two hemispheres: the lower half smooth cream-white glazed stone, the upper half deep teal enamel. A thick polished brass equator band runs all the way around where the halves meet, with a round chunky brass-ringed centre button on the front that has a softly glowing pale-cyan inner disc. Subtle shallow carved rune grooves and swirl glyphs etched into both hemispheres. The orb rests upright on a tiny flat area at the bottom of the sphere. Diameter about 0.30 m. Stylised Palworld / Animo-class game item prop, deliberately chunky and oversized, exaggerated readable silhouette that still reads clearly from 10-15 metres, soft bevelled edges, soft hand-painted PBR look, natural palette matching the Meadows key-art reference (sage and leaf greens, warm gold, cream, slate blue, teal). Single isolated object standing upright on its flat base, full object visible and centred, plain neutral light-grey background, even studio lighting, no cast shadow, no ground plane, no people, no creatures, no text, no letters, no labels, no red or crimson anywhere.
concepts.verdict: CHOSEN (views 1-2): teal upper and cream lower hemispheres, ornate brass equator band, brass-ringed glowing cyan centre button, carved runes and swirls; view 0 rejected for 3D because it showed button-like knobs on both sides, inconsistent with views 1-2

agent_visual_verdict: Good: deep teal upper and cream lower hemispheres, ornate brass equator band, chunky brass-ringed centre button with pale cyan disc (intended glow zone; no emissive map, add emissive at integration), carved runes on the teal half (shallow, mostly in texture). A matching button sits on the back. Small flat foot at the bottom. Rune glyphs resemble futhark letters, not words. 0.30 m sphere.
palette_check: teal, cream and brass only; no red/oxblood
integration_status: raw candidate, not imported; OFF until its scene passes three-judge review
